lang.unreviewed: This translation has not been reviewed by a native speaker. The English page is authoritative:
lead.platforms: Test counts per Kotlin target and CI host.
lead.interop: Kuicksilver's Ktor engines against other clients and servers, per wire protocol; the QUIC Interop Runner.
lead.conformance: h2spec, h3spec and Autobahn: what runs in CI and what does not yet.
lead.fuzzing: Fuzz targets, committed corpora, the regression run and the latest campaign.
lead.sizes: What the published artifacts weigh, per platform.
lead.benchmarks: Throughput and handshake measurements, with where and when they were taken.
lead.rfc: Requirements met, partly met, planned and not planned, from the RFC compliance matrix.
lead.how: The checks every change goes through, and how to verify a release yourself.
index.intro: Every number on these pages is generated from the CI results of the commit this documentation was built from; nothing is typed in by hand. A section with no result for this commit says so.
prov.none: No successful CI run was found for commit {sha}: the sections that come from CI show no data.
prov.run: Data from the successful build.yml run of commit {sha}, started {date}.
nodata.run: No data: there is no CI run for this commit.
nodata.lane: No data: the CI run of this commit produced no result for this section.
platforms.intro: One row per Kotlin target and the CI host it ran on. A test run counts every test case of every module of that target.
platforms.compiledOnly: (compiled in CI; there is no iOS device to run the tests on)
platforms.note: The JVM suites run on several hosts and JDKs; each row is a separate run, so the same test is counted once per row.
interop.intro: Kuicksilver's Ktor client and server engines against Ktor's Netty and CIO engines, OkHttp, the JDK's HttpClient and Netty's HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 codecs, in one JVM over loopback. The cases and the findings are described in
interop.unmapped: {n} test cases have no pair in tools/docs/engine-pairs.tsv and are not shown.
interop.runnerNone: Not run for this commit: the QUIC Interop Runner matrix runs weekly and on request, not on every commit.
conformance.intro: Third-party test suites that check a protocol implementation against its specification.
conformance.local: h2spec runs in CI on the linuxX64 server and in the local release gate (tools/interop/h2spec.sh; every case must pass); earlier results, with the JVM and macOS servers, are recorded in
fuzzing.intro: {targets} fuzz targets exercise the parsers of the TLS, QUIC, HTTP/3 and HTTP/2 layers and of the C shim (Jazzer on the JVM, libFuzzer for C).
fuzzing.regressionCount: The fuzz test classes replay the committed corpora and reproducers on every CI run: {tests} test cases, {failed} failed.
fuzzing.campaignThis: Campaign columns: the fuzz.yml run of this commit ({sha}), started {date}, concluded {conclusion}.
fuzzing.campaignOther: Campaign columns: the latest fuzz.yml run, on another commit ({sha}), started {date}, concluded {conclusion}. It is not a result of this commit.
fuzzing.mutationNone: Not measured in CI: mutation testing is run by hand on selected modules, and the gaps it finds become tests. There is no mutation score to show.
sizes.intro: Sizes of the artifacts the CI run of this commit built.
sizes.android: Android AAR and its native libraries
sizes.klib: Kotlin/Native klibs (unpacked size, sum of the published modules' klibs and cinterop klibs)
sizes.iosNone: No data: the CI run of this commit built no Kuicksilver.xcframework.
benchmarks.intro: How the measurements are taken, and how to read them:
benchmarks.perfNone: No perf.yml run for this commit: perf.yml is started by hand, since goodput on shared CI runners is too noisy for every commit.
benchmarks.committedNote: Measured on a developer machine on {date} at commit {sha}, not in CI; the environment is described in
rfc.intro: Generated from the RFC compliance matrix of this commit. Every ✅ row names the tests that pin it, which a repository check enforces.
rfc.none: The RFC compliance matrix was not found.
rfc.open: Rows that are not fully met
how.intro: Every change goes through the same steps; each link goes to the section of the process document that describes it.
how.step0: A test that fails before the fix
how.step1: Review of the code against the RFC text
how.step2: The RFC compliance matrix and the threat model
how.step3: Integration and the local gate on every platform
how.step4: Hosted CI (the results on these pages)
how.step5: Before a release: soak tests, fuzzing, benchmarks
how.release: To check that the artifacts you download are the ones released, and that the native libraries are what the tagged sources build, see
how.source: The process document is the single source; this page only links to it:
sizes.iosNote: Kuicksilver.xcframework as the Swift package ships it: the dynamic framework binary of each slice is what an app embeds, the zip is what SwiftPM downloads. Kuicksilver's share of a linked app, by origin, is measured with tools/check/ios-size.sh.
prov.expired: The successful build.yml run of commit {sha}, started {date}, is known, but its results are no longer available (CI artifacts are kept 30 days): the sections that come from CI show no data.
benchmarks.perfConclusion: perf.yml run {id} of this commit concluded {conclusion}.
